accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: How testee works for people with disabilities, what falls short, and how to tell us.
accessibility.intro: We want everyone to be able to use testee: to take an interview a company sends you, to practise, and to run a company's hiring. We aim to meet level AA of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2.

done.title: What we do
done.themes: Light and dark themes: your device's setting by default, or light or dark if you pick one.
done.contrast: Colors a company chooses for its interview pages are refused when text on them would be hard to read (below WCAG contrast).
done.languages: The site in 23 languages, right to left where the language is written that way.
done.phones: Pages fit phone screens and work when you zoom in.
done.text: Interview questions are shown as text with answer options, also in voice mode, where you can tap instead of speaking.
done.extraTime: A company can give you extra time on each question. Ask the company for it, or for another accommodation, before you start; you don't have to say why. If you came through a shareable link, ask for a personal invite first: extra time can't be added to a link.
done.keyboard: From the keyboard: a "Skip to content" link comes first on every page, tabs move with the arrow keys, and screen readers announce a form's errors.

limits.title: What falls short
limits.timed: Interview questions are timed, as the company's assessment requires. If you need more time, ask the company for extra time before you start.
limits.audit: testee hasn't been audited independently yet, so some parts may not meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
limits.providers: Paying for credits (Paddle's checkout), the "I'm not a robot" check (Cloudflare Turnstile) and the video on the home page (YouTube) are run by those providers, under their own accessibility.
limits.voice: An interview in voice mode needs your microphone and sound allowed before you start, even if you'll tap your answers. If you can't use them, ask the company to set you to answering by tapping.

feedback.title: Tell us
feedback.text: If something on testee is hard for you to use, or you need it in another form, write to <email></email>. We answer within 14 days.
feedback.authority: If you aren't satisfied with our answer, you can contact the Estonian Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (TTJA).

trust.title: Trust and security
trust.description: How testee keeps hiring data secure and private: EU hosting, sub-processors, retention, and what we provide for the GDPR, the EU AI Act, the UK and the US.
trust.intro: What testee does to keep your data and your candidates' data safe, where it is stored, who processes it, how long it is kept, and what we give companies for the hiring laws they follow.

security.title: Security
security.signIn: You sign in with Google, LinkedIn or GitHub through Firebase Authentication, so testee stores no passwords. Every request's sign-in is checked on the server.
security.encryption: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2 or later) and at rest. Keys and tokens a company connects (its applicant tracking system, Slack, web hooks) are stored encrypted, and testee API keys only as a one-way hash.
security.access: Every request is checked against the company and the role of the person making it. Each service reaches only its own database, and calls between services are signed.
security.limits: Rate limits protect every action that costs money or can be abused, and an "I'm not a robot" check guards public forms, job ad links and creating a first company.
security.logs: Error reports leave out email addresses, and server logs are kept briefly.
security.actionLog: A company's owner sees an action log of who did what in the company, and when.
security.backups: The database is backed up every day, with point-in-time recovery for the last 7 days.
security.breaches: If a company's data is ever breached, we tell the company without undue delay, within 48 hours where we can.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.roles: testee is the controller of the accounts of the people who use it, and a processor of candidates' data, which belongs to the company that invites them.
privacy.noSelling: We don't sell personal data or share it for advertising. There are no advertising or analytics cookies.
privacy.noInference: testee collects no data about candidates' sex, age, origin or disability, and infers nothing of the kind.
privacy.voice: In voice mode, a candidate's spoken answer is turned into text and matched to the options, and the option it matched is said back to them and shown on screen; an answer to a question with several right options is confirmed first. testee stores no speech, and the voice isn't analysed in any other way. OpenAI, which turns it into text, may keep it for up to 30 days, as below.
privacy.ai: OpenAI, which writes the questions, is told not to store what it receives where its API offers that choice; it may keep the data for up to 30 days, only to check for abuse unless the law requires longer, and doesn't use it to train its models.
privacy.rights: Anyone can download or delete their own data in Settings, without writing to us.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.aiAct: Under the EU AI Act, testee is treated as a high-risk AI system, whose duties apply from <time>{date}</time>. Our instructions for companies are its instructions for use.
compliance.aiMarks: Questions, answer options, the assistant's answers and voice clips are marked as AI-generated in a form software can read: data-ai-generated in a page's code, and the AI_GENERATED tag in a voice clip's file. Voice clips also carry OpenAI's inaudible watermark, which you can check at <verify>openai.com/verify</verify>. Text copied from a page doesn't keep its mark.
compliance.humanReview: testee makes no decision about a candidate: people at the company review the results and decide, and candidates can ask for a person to review their result.
compliance.dpa: The data processing agreement is part of the terms, with nothing to sign. It covers the GDPR, the UK GDPR, and US state privacy laws such as California's, where testee is the company's service provider.
compliance.documents: Companies get <link>instructions for use, a DPIA template and candidate notice templates</link>, with versions for New York City, Illinois and Colorado.
compliance.nyc: New York City: before using testee for a role there, the employer does what Local Law 144 asks of it: an independent bias audit within the year before use, its summary published, and a notice to candidates who live in the city at least 10 business days before they are assessed. testee's own independent bias audit is done before <time>{date}</time>, and every year after.

residency.title: Where data is stored
residency.storage: testee runs on Google Cloud in the EU, in Belgium, where its database is stored. Rate-limit counters are kept at Upstash, also in Belgium. Emails are sent from Ireland through Resend, which stores them in the United States.
residency.transfers: Four providers handle data in the United States: Google for sign-in, OpenAI, Resend for emails, and Cloudflare for the "I'm not a robot" check. Mail in our Google Workspace inbox may also be stored outside the EU. These transfers are covered by the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, and for the UK by the UK Extension and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum.

voice.title: Voice mode with Mira
voice.text: Mira, an AI interviewer, reads each question and its options aloud, and candidates answer hands-free. A clear answer is saved at once; anything else is confirmed first.
voice.alt: A voice interview: Mira, the AI interviewer, beside the question, with the turn pill showing it's the candidate's turn.

brand.title: Your brand, not ours
brand.text: Set your logo, colors for light and dark, fonts and corners, with a live preview. Candidates see only your company, without testee's header or footer.
brand.alt: The brand tab's colors for the page, buttons and fills, with a live preview of the interview.

candidates.title: Compare candidates at a glance
candidates.text: Every candidate's status and grade against your passing grade, in one list. Sort by grade, search by name or email, filter by who passed or who's flagged.
candidates.alt: An interview's candidates list with names, statuses, grades and a flagged candidate.

signals.title: Integrity signals
signals.text: Page leaves, copy attempts and answers too fast to have been read, plus two answer patterns: times that don't follow the questions, and hard questions right while easy ones are wrong.
signals.alt: A candidate's report: the answer patterns card with its signals and suggested follow-up questions.

share.title: Share reports in seconds
share.text: Download a PDF for one candidate or the whole interview, email it from testee, or send a short summary in a messenger.
share.alt: The share dialog for a candidate's report: an email address to send the PDF to, or a summary in WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or LINE.

notes.title: Notes for your team
notes.text: Write about the hiring round on the interview's notes tab and pin the note that matters: it shows under the interview's name. Candidates never see notes.
notes.alt: An interview's notes tab with a pinned note and a newer note from the team.

emails.title: Emails that do the work
emails.text: Candidates get their invitation in the interview's language, with your logo, and a reminder if they haven't started. Your team gets one daily digest instead of an email for every event.
emails.alt: An interview invitation email from Lumen Health, with its logo and the button that opens the invite

integrations.title: Every connection in one place
integrations.text: Connect an ATS, Slack, API keys, web hooks and AI apps from your company's integrations tab, each with its own page and steps.
integrations.alt: A company's integrations tab: a connected ATS, Slack, the API, web hooks and AI apps.

biasAudit.title: Bias-audit export
biasAudit.text: Export finished candidates' results as a CSV for an independent bias audit, such as New York City's Local Law 144, or your own four-fifths check.
biasAudit.alt: The bias-audit export dialog: all interviews or one, and an optional date range.

points.options: Four options per question, some with more than one right answer
points.examples: Code, data, formulas or documents shown as examples where the role needs them
points.names: Lines that can't be invited are named, with the reason
points.credits: Credits come back for anyone who never answers
points.expire: Invites expire on their own after a month
points.signIn: Candidates sign in with the email you invited, so a forwarded invite is no use to anyone else
points.linkOff: Turned off at any time, and when the role is hired
points.mode: Click or voice mode chosen on the same page
points.settings: Average time per question and passing grade beside it
points.time: The total time shown before they start
points.phone: Works on a phone as well as a computer
points.onePass: One attempt: no going back, no retakes
points.tap: Tapping an option always works too
points.kept: testee keeps no voice: it's only turned into text
points.voiceLanguages: In all 23 languages, with quality that varies by language
points.contrast: Colors that would be hard to read are refused
points.logo: Your logo on invitations, the interview and PDF reports
points.sort: Best grades first in one click
points.status: Invited, in process, finished, expired or undelivered
points.proof: A reason to look closer, never proof
points.camera: No camera, screen recording or device tracking
points.followUps: Questions to talk through in a live interview
points.pdf: PDF reports with grades and every answer
points.messengers: Summaries on WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or LINE
points.bell: New notes reach the bell and your Slack channel
points.atsList: Workable, Greenhouse, Teamtailor, Recruitee and Breezy HR
points.results: Candidates invited automatically, results sent back
points.docs: Developer docs for the API, web hooks, the SDK and MCP
points.noInference: testee never asks for or guesses protected characteristics
points.owner: Only the owner exports, and it's in the action log
points.askTime: Anyone who needs more time is told to ask before starting
points.peopleDecide: Told that people at your company review the results and decide
points.digest: The digest: who finished, undelivered invites, ATS candidates not invited, new notes and interviews ready
points.emailChoice: The digest, reminders, news and offers turned on or off in your settings
points.stopEmails: Candidates can stop your emails in one click

templates.title: Ready-made templates
templates.text: Copy an interview by role, level and language, at once and free.

bank.title: Shared question bank
bank.text: New interviews reuse questions proven in others. Keep an interview's questions out with one switch.

quality.title: Questions that fix themselves
quality.text: Answers, votes and reports flag weak questions; they're fixed or replaced.

languages.title: {count, plural, one {# language} other {# languages}}
languages.text: The app, the interviews and the emails, in your candidates' language.

preview.title: Preview it first
preview.text: Take the interview as a candidate would, for free, before inviting anyone.

manage.title: Manage questions
manage.text: Read every question, disable one, re-generate it or mark its answer as wrong.

ats.title: From your ATS
ats.text: Candidates at the stage you pick are invited automatically, and results go back.

platform.title: From your platform
platform.text: Invite through the API, or embed the interview in your own site with the SDK.

assistants.title: From an AI assistant
assistants.text: Ask Mira, or Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps over MCP, with your permissions.

extraTime.title: Extra time
extraTime.text: Give a candidate more time on each question before they start; no reason asked.

ownMode.title: Their own mode
ownMode.text: Switch one candidate to click or voice mode, for someone who can't answer aloud.

fair.title: The same rules for all
fair.text: The same timer and mix of questions for everyone, with the clock kept by the server.

rate.title: Candidates rate questions
rate.text: A vote and a way to report a problem on every question.

accessible.title: Accessible
accessible.text: Built for WCAG 2.2 AA, in every language, light and dark.

practice.title: Free practice
practice.text: Anyone can practise by role, free and in private, and see every right answer at the end.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.text: The bell, emails and your Slack channel tell you when candidates finish.

discover.title: Discover
discover.text: Once you've topped up, see people open to offers whose free practice matches the role.

hired.title: Mark as hired
hired.text: Close the role and its shareable link in one step.

search.title: Search everything
search.text: One search in the header finds your companies, interviews and candidates, and every page, guide and skills test.

slack.title: Slack
slack.text: Pick a channel and which notifications go there.

api.title: Public API
api.text: Keys with only the permissions you tick, optionally limited to your IP addresses.

webhooks.title: Web hooks
webhooks.text: Signed events when a candidate starts or finishes, with a test send and a delivery log.

mcp.title: AI apps over MCP
mcp.text: Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps read and act with your permissions.

mira.title: Ask Mira
mira.text: The AI assistant reads your results, answers how-tos and acts once you confirm.

person.title: A person decides
person.text: The score supports your decision; it doesn't make it.

roles.title: Team roles
roles.text: Members are free. Only the owner manages the team; viewers see results, share reports and write notes, and spend nothing.

companies.title: Several companies
companies.text: One account can own several companies, each with its own team and credits.

log.title: Action log
log.text: The owner sees who did what, in the app, through Mira, an AI app, the API or an ATS.

documents.title: Documents ready
documents.text: A data processing agreement, a DPIA template and candidate notice templates.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.text: No selling of data, nothing inferred about candidates, no voice kept by testee.

location.title: Stored in Belgium
location.text: On Google Cloud in the EU; the trust page lists every provider.

retention.title: Deleted on time
retention.text: Results go 12 months after the last invitation, or at once when you revoke a candidate.

verified.title: Verified companies
verified.text: A check next to your company's name once a work email on its website and our review confirm it.

free.title: {count, plural, one {# free candidate} other {# free candidates}}
free.text: Your first company starts with them, no card needed.

answered.title: Only who answers
answered.text: Unanswered invites cost nothing; their credits come back.

expire.title: Credits never expire
expire.text: Larger top-ups cost less per candidate; unused paid credits are refundable within 14 days.

autoTopUp.title: Automatic top-up
autoTopUp.text: Optional: credits refilled when they run low, still no subscription.

referrals.title: Referrals
referrals.text: Bring another company and you both get free candidates once it tops up.

currencies.title: Your currency
currencies.text: Prices in {count, plural, one {# currency} other {# currencies}}, set by your country.

closing.title:
Create your first interview
It's free

hiringFlow.title: Hiring flow
hiringFlow.description: Every step of hiring with testee, from the job description you paste to the report you share and the hire you make.

hero.title:
from job description
to the right hire
hero.text: Every step of hiring with testee, and every option at each one: follow the line down.

describe.title: Describe the job
describe.text: Paste a job description, or start from a ready template. Any role, any field, in any of 23 languages.
describe.alt: The new interview page with a job description pasted

topics.title: Review the topics
topics.text: testee proposes the topics the job needs. You keep, rename, add or remove them, set their subtopics and approve.
topics.alt: The topic review: topics with their subtopics, one being edited

questions.title: Questions are generated and checked
questions.text: AI writes a pool of questions for each topic, a second AI checks a sample of answer keys blind, and each candidate gets their own random set.

points.unique: A random set for each candidate
points.checked: A sample of answer keys checked by a second AI
points.bank: Proven questions from the shared bank

questions.alt: A topic's questions, each with its answer key

settings.title: Set it up
settings.text: Choose how long each question takes, the passing grade and how candidates answer, and put the interview in your brand.

invite.title: Invite candidates
invite.text: Bring candidates in the way your hiring already works. Each one is reserved a candidate's credits, given back if they never answer.

points.credits: Credits only for those who answer

email.title: By email
email.text: Type their emails, with names if you like: each gets an invitation with their own link.

list.title: List or file
list.text: Paste a list or upload a CSV or text file to invite up to a hundred at once.

link.title: Link in job ad
link.text: Turn on the shareable link and anyone who applies takes the interview, once each.

ats.title: From your ATS
ats.text: Connect Greenhouse, Workable, Teamtailor, Recruitee or Breezy HR: moving a candidate to a stage invites them.

api.title: Your platform
api.text: Invite through the API, or embed the interview in your own site with the SDK.

ai.title: Mira or AI app
ai.text: Ask Mira, or Claude, ChatGPT or another AI app, to invite candidates for you.

candidate.title: Candidates take it
candidate.text: Candidates see the rules and the time up front, give their word, and answer one timed question at a time, by click or by voice, on any device.

points.extraTime: Extra time for those who need it

candidate.alt: A question in click mode with two options ticked

results.title: See who's best
results.text: Every candidate's score and answers as soon as they finish, with signals worth a closer look and your team's notes.
results.alt: An interview's candidates, with their statuses and grades

share.title: Share the reports
share.text: Send a candidate's report to whoever decides, in the way they read it, and keep your tools up to date.

email.title: By email
email.text: Send the PDF report to whoever decides, inside or outside your team.

chat.title: In a chat
chat.text: Share a short summary on WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or LINE.

ats.title: Back to your ATS
ats.text: Each result goes back to the candidate in your ATS as a note.

slack.title: To Slack
slack.text: Your channel hears when candidates finish, and the notifications you pick.

webhooks.title: Web hooks
webhooks.text: Your systems get every finished candidate's result as it happens.

decide.title: Decide and hire
decide.text: People decide, never the AI. Mark the role hired to close its link, and keep the records your hiring law asks for.
decide.alt: A candidate's report with a passing grade
